newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SEES 1997 SUGAR BEET OUTPUT SHARPLY HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SEES 1997 SUGAR BEET OUTPUT SHARPLY HIGHER.

text.p: Bulgaria's agriculture ministry said on Wednesday 8,000 hectares would be planted with sugar beet in 1997 and forecast an output of 120,000 tonnes, compared to 53,000 in 1996.
A ministry plan set the sugar beet area at 8,000 ha, up from last year's 6,000, but still far below 1995's beet area of 11,200 ha.

"I consider the figures realistic and I hope there will be a sharp rise of output this year in comparison with the previous which was catastrophic for the sector," the Sugar Institute's chief agronomist Nikolai Dobrev told Reuters.
Bulgaria's sugar output fell by 64 percent in 1996 due to bad weather in the spring. Farmers had difficulties obtaining funds due to the general economic crisis in the country.
Dobrev said they were trying to attract more private growers and farming co-operatives to the sector and there was a big interest due to rising unemployment.

"We are trying to create incentives to farmers, like free supplies of sugar for instance, which we hope will provide greater care and hence bigger yield," Dobrev said. "I hope last year's situation will not be repeated."

But even with the expected higher output Bulgaria, which used to meet nearly 50 percent of its sugar needs with local production, is expected to supply its sugar-processing plants with less than 10 percent of their needs.
